findings.mechanism: Blocking CPU‑bound pbkdf2Sync call runs on the Node event‑loop thread, violating the async concurrency model (03-concurrency-models) and causing all other requests to wait, inflating latency.
findings.remediation: Replace crypto.pbkdf2Sync with the asynchronous crypto.pbkdf2 and use fs.promises.writeFile instead of writeFileSync to avoid blocking the event loop.
findings.arithmetic: pbkdf2Sync with 600 000 iterations ≈200 ms on typical hardware; with N=10 concurrent requests the event loop serialises them, so 99th‑percentile latency ≈N × 200 ms = 2000 ms.

findings.mechanism: Two concurrent calls with the same orderId perform unsynchronised writeFileSync, a classic read‑modify‑write race (04-races-and-atomicity) that can overwrite each other’s output, producing duplicate side‑effects.
findings.remediation: Serialize writes per orderId (e.g., a mutex or atomic rename pattern) or include a unique suffix in the filename to avoid collisions.
findings.arithmetic: With two concurrent invocations the function executes twice, but only one file persists; the extra write counts as one duplicate side‑effect.
